question: What do we call the temporary germs you pick up while touching patients that cause most hospital infections?

options.A: Transient flora
options.B: Fungal spores
options.C: Endogenous flora
options.D: Resident flora

explanation: Transient flora are just passing through! You pick them up during patient care, and thankfully, regular hand washing easily washes them away. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why is nurse safety considered just as important as patient safety?

options.A: Healthy and protected nurses provide better care and prevent errors
options.B: Hospital management is only legally liable for nurse injuries
options.C: Patients cannot recover unless nurses take daily rest breaks
options.D: Nurses pay for hospital equipment out of their own salaries

explanation: When nurses are safe from burnout, injuries, and infections, they remain alert and capable of delivering high-quality, error-free care to patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h1)

question: How do the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways work together in the body?

options.A: They both activate a series of clotting factors that lead into the common pathway
options.B: They regulate the exact volume of blood pumped by the heart
options.C: They prevent platelets from sticking to healthy blood vessels
options.D: They work in opposite directions to dissolve unwanted blood clots

explanation: Both pathways act as separate starting points that eventually feed into the same shared sequence to produce a solid clot. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: What would happen if the hypothalamus released GnRH in a steady, continuous stream instead of in pulses?

options.A: It would make the pituitary gland grow larger in size
options.B: It would immediately trigger strong bone growth in the arms
options.C: It would stop reproductive stimulation instead of promoting it
options.D: It would cause puberty to happen twice as fast

explanation: Exactly! The pituitary gland needs short, repeating pulses of GnRH to stay active. If the signal is non-stop, it actually shuts the process down. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T13#GNS121_U5_T13_h2)

question: At what tier of government is primary health care and public health nursing primarily managed in Nigeria?

options.A: Local government level
options.B: International embassy level
options.C: Global health organization level
options.D: Private corporate level

explanation: Nigeria's primary health care system is decentralized and managed primarily at the local government area level. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why do heavy blocks of text usually fail in community health education programs?

options.A: People prefer listening to long audio recordings instead.
options.B: Ink tends to smudge when paragraphs are printed too close together.
options.C: Medical authorities forbid the use of written sentences on posters.
options.D: Low literacy rates in the target population make reading difficult.

explanation: Many community members have limited reading skills. If your poster is packed with heavy text, the main health message gets lost. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h3)

question: During natural family planning, what does a woman look for when checking her cervical mucus for peak fertility?

options.A: A thick, sticky discharge that remains present all month
options.B: A brownish bloody discharge right before ovulation
options.C: Complete dryness with no vaginal secretions at all
options.D: Clear, stretchy mucus that looks like raw egg white

explanation: Think of raw egg whites! When ovulation approaches, the mucus changes texture to help sperm swim easily toward the egg. Simple and natural! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h2)

question: How is a nursing manager's decision different from the choices you make at a patient's bedside?

options.A: Writing individual nursing care plans
options.B: Treating one specific patient at a time
options.C: Performing physical examinations
options.D: Affecting entire units, staff, and budgets

explanation: At the bedside, you focus on one patient at a time. But as a manager, your decisions ripple across the whole ward, affecting staff duties and hospital resources! [learn more](GST321_U1_T8#GST321_U1_T8_h1)

question: How does cognitivism view how our minds handle learning?

options.A: As an emotional center completely separate from memory
options.B: As an active information processor similar to a computer
options.C: As a blank slate that only reacts to external rewards
options.D: As a muscle that only grows through physical exercise

explanation: Think of your brain like a smart computer: it takes in data, processes it, stores it safely, and pulls it back out when you need it on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h3)

question: Where do most traditional food beliefs and taboos originally come from?

options.A: From ancient survival experiences and local observations
options.B: From strict international food safety laws
options.C: From textbooks written by professional dietitians
options.D: From modern laboratory experiments conducted by scientists

explanation: Many food rules started long ago as clever ways to protect people from perceived dangers or explain natural events. History and culture run deep in our communities! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h2)

question: About how long are the intestines in an adult human body when fully stretched out?

options.A: Fifteen meters
options.B: Two meters
options.C: Nine meters
options.D: One meter

explanation: It sounds unbelievable because they fit inside our belly, but our intestines stretch to about nine meters long! You've got this. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T4#GNS121_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary function of luteinizing hormone in the male reproductive system?

options.A: Stimulating testosterone production in the testes
options.B: Directly forming the flagellum of maturing sperm
options.C: Neutralizing acidic fluid in the male urethra
options.D: Lowering body temperature inside the scrotal sac

explanation: Luteinizing hormone targets specific cells in the testes to trigger the synthesis and release of testosterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the leading underlying medical condition that weakens bones and causes low-impact fractures?

options.A: Osteoarthritis
options.B: Atherosclerosis
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Osteoporosis

explanation: Osteoporosis reduces bone mass and density, making the skeleton fragile and prone to breaking from minor bumps or normal daily activities. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which common bacterial infection is famous for causing silent damage that can lead to infertility if ignored?

options.A: Candidiasis
options.B: Chlamydia
options.C: Pubic lice
options.D: Bacterial vaginosis

explanation: Chlamydia is often called a 'silent' infection because it sneaks in without symptoms while quietly harming the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which clinical encounter offers nurses a key opportunity to identify victims of early marriage?

options.A: Annual hospital administration meetings
options.B: Surgical safety checklist briefings
options.C: Routine occupational health screenings
options.D: Antenatal and maternity clinic visits

explanation: Young pregnant girls frequently interact with maternity nurses, making prenatal clinics ideal settings for identifying underage and coerced unions. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h5)

question: A patient cannot move their left eye outward. Which cranial nerve nucleus in the pons is likely involved?

options.A: Trochlear nucleus
options.B: Abducens nucleus
options.C: Oculomotor nucleus
options.D: Facial nucleus

explanation: The abducens nerve (CN VI) controls the lateral rectus muscle, which pulls the eye outward. Clinical neurology made simple! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h2)

question: Why do patients still need supportive care (like IV fluids and oxygen) even after getting an antidote?

options.A: Antidotes usually worsen the patient's baseline vital signs
options.B: Supportive care keeps the patient stable while the body handles the toxin
options.C: Supportive care replaces the need for any toxicological screening
options.D: Antidotes are completely ineffective without continuous intravenous fluids

explanation: Antidotes are amazing, but they aren't instant magic. Supportive care keeps the patient breathing and stable while the antidote and the body do the heavy lifting to clear the poison. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h1)

question: What does the brain's central chemoreceptor primarily monitor to control breathing?

options.A: Total volume of blood pumped per minute by the left ventricle
options.B: Concentration of glucose dissolved in blood plasma
options.C: Direct measurements of iron levels in circulating red blood cells
options.D: Changes in pH and carbon dioxide levels in cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Central chemoreceptors act like chemical sensors, checking the fluid around the brain for pH and carbon dioxide to decide how fast you need to breathe. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T14#GNS211_U3_T14_h5)

question: Why do doctors order diagnostic tests in reproductive health?

options.A: To permanently cure all chronic reproductive tract infections
options.B: To replace the need for a physical clinical examination
options.C: To induce immediate menopause in older female patients
options.D: To investigate underlying structural or hormonal abnormalities

explanation: Spot on! Diagnostic tests help us figure out the root cause of any structural, hormonal, or functional issues in the reproductive system. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h1)

question: Poor drainage and overcrowding in a neighborhood are examples of which part of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Environment
options.B: Agent
options.C: Immunity
options.D: Host

explanation: Well done! Surroundings, living conditions, and sanitation factors make up the 'environment' part of the triangle, which greatly influences how diseases spread. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h2)

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the soft spot towards the front of a baby's head)?

options.A: Triangle
options.B: Square
options.C: Circle
options.D: Diamond

explanation: The anterior fontanelle is famously diamond-shaped. This is a classic midwife clue that helps you tell it apart from the triangular posterior fontanelle during an exam! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h3)

question: In nursing research, what do we actually mean by 'measurement'?

options.A: Recording vital signs only during morning rounds
options.B: Assigning numbers or labels to objects or events
options.C: Prescribing medication according to hospital policy
options.D: Treating patients based on their personal preferences

explanation: Think of measurement simply as giving a number or a clear label to something we are observing, following a set of rules. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T1#GNS217_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why do hospitals require standard precautions for every single patient, no matter their diagnosis?

options.A: Infectious diseases only spread after a laboratory confirms them
options.B: It saves time so nurses do not have to check patient charts
options.C: Patients prefer knowing their care involves extra safety steps
options.D: Any patient's blood or body fluid can carry hidden infectious pathogens

explanation: You can't always tell who has an infection by looking at them. Treating every body fluid as potentially infectious keeps you safe every time. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h6)

question: How do home-based care programs help patients with advanced HIV disease?

options.A: By diagnosing new infectious diseases without laboratory testing equipment
options.B: By replacing the need for antiretroviral medications entirely with herbal remedies
options.C: By providing family-supported nursing care, hygiene assistance, and monitoring at home
options.D: By isolating patients from their families so they never leave the bedroom

explanation: Home-based care brings comfort right to the doorstep, helping families manage daily nursing care, hygiene, and spotting any new symptoms early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h9)

question: What happens when the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to close properly?

options.A: Air builds up rapidly in the upper airway
options.B: Digestive enzymes destroy the small intestine
options.C: Swallowed food gets trapped in the throat
options.D: Stomach acid flows backward into the tube

explanation: Think of this sphincter as a one-way gate. When it stays loose, irritating stomach contents can easily splash back upward, causing that familiar burning feeling. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary fluid transported within the lymphatic system?

options.A: Plasma
options.B: Lymph
options.C: Serum
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: Lymph is the clear fluid collected from interstitial spaces that travels through the lymphatic vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: What is the big advantage of partnering with local transport unions during a disaster?

options.A: Financing the national budget for disaster management
options.B: Securing vehicles quickly for evacuation and relief supply delivery
options.C: Exempting commercial drivers from all traffic laws permanently
options.D: Allowing union members to take over government leadership roles

explanation: Spot on! Transport unions have plenty of vehicles and know the local shortcuts, which speeds up evacuations and getting supplies where they need to go. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the main job of a problem statement in your research proposal?

options.A: To provide a summary of the statistical results
options.B: To explain the background and why the issue needs attention
options.C: To offer final medical advice to patients
options.D: To list the personal biographies of the researchers

explanation: The problem statement tells your reader: 'Here is what is going wrong, here is why it matters, and here is why we need to fix it right now.' [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which supplement is given to pregnant women to help prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Potassium chloride
options.C: Zinc gluconate
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Folic acid is a super important vitamin during early pregnancy. It helps the baby's brain and spinal cord develop properly. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h3)

question: A patient runs their fingers over rough fabric to feel the texture. Which skin receptor is working hardest here?

options.A: Ruffini endings
options.B: Thermoreceptors
options.C: Merkel disks
options.D: Pacinian corpuscles

explanation: Well done! Merkel disks are close to the surface and give your brain wonderful, detailed feedback about shapes, edges, and rough textures. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h3)

question: Why might a patient in early shock still have a normal blood pressure reading?

options.A: Blood pressure monitors are usually inaccurate in emergencies
options.B: Kidneys immediately stop producing urine to save pressure
options.C: Fluid volume only affects the health of the heart
options.D: The body uses compensatory mechanisms like vasoconstriction

explanation: Our amazing bodies fight back! The nervous system tightens blood vessels and speeds up the heart to keep blood pressure normal at first, even if fluid is low. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h4)

question: How does preventing a hospital-acquired infection help save money?

options.A: It shortens hospital stays and reduces extra treatment costs
options.B: It allows the hospital to fire half of its clinical staff
options.C: It completely eliminates all indirect overhead expenses
options.D: It shifts patient care expenses entirely to the government

explanation: Preventing complications saves money naturally because patients get well faster, needing fewer drugs, fewer tests, and shorter bed days. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why do many women experience sudden hair loss a few months after giving birth?

options.A: Breastfeeding drains all essential proteins from the scalp
options.B: Stored-up hairs from the growth phase shed all at once as hormones drop
options.C: Washing hair too frequently damages the weak hair roots
options.D: Newborn care stress permanently destroys hair follicles

explanation: During pregnancy, thick hormones hold onto your hair. Once those hormones drop after birth, all that extra hair decides to take a break and shed at once! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h4)

question: What are the two main components that make up the cardiovascular system?

options.A: The brain and spinal cord
options.B: The heart and blood vessels
options.C: The lungs and airways
options.D: The kidneys and bladder

explanation: The cardiovascular system is composed of the heart, which acts as the pump, and blood vessels, which serve as the delivery pipes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of these represents secondary healthcare in Nigeria?

options.A: Private herbal research institutes
options.B: General and state specialist hospitals
options.C: Local village health posts
options.D: Federal university teaching hospitals

explanation: General hospitals and state specialist hospitals are our go-to secondary facilities, offering different specialty departments to care for admitted patients. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h3)

question: What do the intervals or 'bins' on the horizontal axis represent in a histogram?

options.A: The specific dates when the study ended
options.B: Randomly selected patient interview questions
options.C: Different hospital wards in the facility
options.D: Equal numerical ranges of the measured variable

explanation: Bins cut the continuous scale into neat, equal slices so you can easily count and compare your data. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an anthropometric measurement?

options.A: Daily water consumption
options.B: Body mass index
options.C: Serum albumin level
options.D: Blood pressure reading

explanation: You've got this! Anthropometric just means measuring physical body dimensions like height, weight, and BMI. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h3)

question: Which blood type is known as the universal red blood cell donor because it has no A or B antigens?

options.A: Type O
options.B: Type A
options.C: Type AB
options.D: Type B

explanation: Correct! Because Type O red blood cells don't carry A or B antigens, a recipient's immune system won't easily attack them during emergencies. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T1#GNS311_U2_T1_h7)

question: What does the 'impersonal' aspect of the Hot Stove Rule mean?

options.A: Discipline targets the behavior, not the person
options.B: Rules apply only to new nursing staff members
options.C: Managers should never speak to the nurse directly
options.D: Penalties are handed out by a computer program

explanation: Fair discipline focuses purely on what the worker did wrong rather than attacking who they are. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a reason why some families might hide a sick relative from home care providers?

options.A: Belief that family care is a strict moral obligation
options.B: Stigma associated with certain chronic or mental illnesses
options.C: Fear of community gossip and social judgment
options.D: Desire to follow strict hospital discharge protocols

explanation: Well done! Families might hide patients due to fear of gossip or stigma, but hospital protocols are never the reason. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the golden rule for feeding an infant during their first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding with no other foods or liquids
options.B: Cow milk combined with fresh fruit juices
options.C: Formula milk mixed with clean local spring water
options.D: Breastmilk supplemented with thin cereal porridges

explanation: You got it! Breastmilk alone for the first six months provides all the nutrients and infection-fighting protection a baby needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h7)

question: Why does someone who has recovered from chickenpox almost never catch it a second time?

options.A: Red blood cells absorb and neutralize the viral particles in the blood
options.B: Innate physical barriers permanently change to block the virus from entering
options.C: Adaptive memory cells remain in the body to recognize the virus immediately
options.D: Stomach acid adapts to destroy the chickenpox virus on contact

explanation: Your body leaves behind 'memory cells' after an infection. If the chickenpox virus dares to show its face again, these memory cells recognize it instantly and crush it! [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the proper term for professional negligence committed by a healthcare provider?

options.A: Insubordination
options.B: Defamation
options.C: Battery
options.D: Malpractice

explanation: Malpractice simply means professional negligence—when a healthcare provider fails to meet the expected standard of care and a patient gets hurt. You will master these terms easily! [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h3)

question: What communication style works best to encourage a patient to adopt healthier eating habits?

options.A: A silent demonstration with no words
options.B: A strict and formal medical lecture
options.C: A rapid list of commands to follow
options.D: A collaborative and supportive dialogue

explanation: Working together through supportive conversation helps patients feel empowered rather than judged or forced. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h4)

question: A postoperative patient has a urine output of 15 mL over the last hour. What does this finding most likely suggest?

options.A: An infection in the urinary bladder
options.B: Overhydration causing the kidneys to shut down
options.C: Inadequate organ perfusion from low blood volume
options.D: A normal reaction to pain medication wearing off

explanation: When blood volume drops, the body reduces blood flow to the kidneys, causing urine production to fall well below normal levels. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main goal of giving a patient a tranquilizer?

options.A: To increase physical energy and alertness
options.B: To lower elevated blood pressure levels
options.C: To reduce anxiety and calm the mind
options.D: To permanently cure chronic depression

explanation: Tranquilizers are given to ease psychological tension and help patients relax without heavy sedation. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T4#GNS223_U6_T4_h1)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient says a warm compress feels like it is burning their skin?

options.A: Press the compress down harder to ensure even contact
options.B: Administer an oral pain medication and leave the compress on
options.C: Remove the compress immediately and inspect the skin
options.D: Wait five minutes to see if the skin adjusts to the heat

explanation: If a patient says it burns, take it off right away and check the skin. Never ignore a burn complaint! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T9#GNS221_U3_T9_h7)

question: Research objectives need to be clear and measurable. What kind of words should they always start with?

options.A: Pronouns
options.B: Action verbs
options.C: Prepositions
options.D: Adjectives

explanation: Always kick off your objectives with active words like 'to evaluate', 'to assess', or 'to compare' so everyone knows exactly what you plan to do. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why must you confirm a bed is ready at the receiving hospital before you even launch the evacuation?

options.A: To ensure the transport vehicle has enough fuel for the trip
options.B: To let the pilot know which runway is clear for landing
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: To prevent dangerous delays upon arrival at the destination

explanation: Arriving at a busy hospital with no bed ready wastes precious time and leaves your vulnerable patient stuck waiting inside the transport vehicle. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h8)

question: What do we call the tiny, milk-producing sacs found inside the breast lobules?

options.A: Alveoli
options.B: Montgomery's tubercles
options.C: Myoepithelial cells
options.D: Lactiferous sinuses

explanation: Think of alveoli as the little factories where breast milk is actually made! They are clustered together inside the breast lobules. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T17#GNS121_U5_T17_h1)

question: What part of a parasitic egg helps it survive harsh outside conditions?

options.A: The tough outer shell
options.B: The internal moving larva
options.C: The flagella tails
options.D: The watery cytoplasm

explanation: That multi-layered outer shell acts like armor, protecting the egg from drying out and handling environmental hazards. Well done! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why is a pregnancy test almost always ordered when a patient arrives with lower belly pain and suspected salpingitis?

options.A: To confirm that the patient is currently using hormonal contraceptives
options.B: To rule out an ectopic pregnancy, which can present with similar pain
options.C: To measure baseline kidney function before starting antibiotic therapy
options.D: To check if high hormone levels caused the bacterial overgrowth

explanation: An ectopic pregnancy is a medical emergency that can mimic pelvic infection pain, so nurses always check this first to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h5)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for maintaining the male accessory glands?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Testosterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Androgens like testosterone control the structure and secretory activity of the accessory reproductive glands. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to conduct nursing research right here in Nigeria instead of relying only on foreign studies?

options.A: Local challenges like resource limits and culture differ from other regions
options.B: Foreign research studies are always fake and poorly written
options.C: Nigerian hospitals are not allowed to read international journals
options.D: International research never deals with patient care issues

explanation: You got it! Solutions have to fit our local Nigerian environment, culture, and available resources to actually work on our wards. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is saliva's main job when you take a bite of food?

options.A: Absorbing simple sugars directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Initiating starch digestion using amylase
options.C: Breaking down complex proteins into amino acids
options.D: Neutralizing stomach acid before swallowing

explanation: Saliva has an enzyme called amylase that immediately starts breaking down starches right inside your mouth. Great job! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h1)

question: How do buildings and public places that aren't wheelchair-friendly affect a person with a physical disability?

options.A: It forces them to rely exclusively on online financial investments
options.B: It encourages them to migrate to rural agricultural communities
options.C: It automatically improves their physical strength through daily climbing
options.D: It prevents them from accessing employment, education, and community events

explanation: Exactly. Physical barriers literally lock people out of schools, jobs, and social life, keeping them from living life to the fullest. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T11#GNS225_U5_T11_h4)

question: What usually causes conductive hearing loss?

options.A: Blockages or problems in the outer or middle ear
options.B: Degeneration of hair cells in the cochlea
options.C: Inability of the brain to process sounds
options.D: Damage to the vestibulocochlear nerve

explanation: Conductive hearing loss simply means something is physically blocking sound waves from traveling through the outer or middle ear—like earwax or fluid. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T14#GNS324_U4_T14_h3)

question: Which serious brain condition can result from severe oxygen deprivation during labour?

options.A: Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy
options.B: Neonatal physiological jaundice
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Transient tachypnoea of the newborn

explanation: Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy is brain damage caused by lack of oxygen and blood flow to the brain around the time of birth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h7)

question: In the ACHES warning acronym for oral contraceptives, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Chest pain
options.B: Cramping
options.C: Constipation
options.D: Coughing

explanation: The ACHES mnemonic is a nursing classic! 'C' stands for chest pain, which can point to serious issues like a blood clot in the lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h7)

question: What is the main reason we teach patients respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette?

options.A: Reducing the cost of cleaning medical equipment
options.B: Preventing foodborne illnesses among patients
options.C: Containing respiratory pathogens at the source
options.D: Purifying the air inside closed hospital wards

explanation: Spot on! Cough etiquette stops germs right where they start—catching them in a tissue or elbow before they can fly into the air. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is fighting social stigma just as important as medical care in HIV prevention?

options.A: Social attitudes are the only proven cause of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
options.B: Stigma causes direct physical mutations in the structure of the HIV virus
options.C: Stigma drives people away from getting tested, seeking counseling, and taking medications
options.D: Overcoming stigma eliminates the need for any safe sex practices

explanation: Spot on! When people fear judgment, they hide from testing and treatment, making the spread harder to control. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h7)

question: Why is a urinalysis always done when checking for stress incontinence?

options.A: To check kidney function and filtration rates
options.B: To measure the exact amount of residual urine left in the bladder
options.C: To test the patient for diabetes and high blood sugar levels
options.D: To rule out a urinary tract infection that can cause similar symptoms

explanation: Infections can mimic incontinence by irritating the bladder, so checking the urine first helps doctors make a clear diagnosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h5)

question: During a vaginal exam, you feel that the baby's skull bones are severely overlapping and jammed tight. What condition might this suggest?

options.A: Premature rupture of membranes
options.B: Normal rapid crowning
options.C: Normal painless descent
options.D: Cephalopelvic disproportion

explanation: Severe, tight overlapping is a sign that the head is struggling to fit through a tight birth canal—a condition we call cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD). Keep this red flag in mind for clinicals! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h6)

question: You are getting an autistic child ready for a blood draw. What nursing action helps lower their anxiety the most?

options.A: Using a visual schedule to show each step of the procedure
options.B: Talking continuously with complex metaphors about bravery
options.C: Performing the procedure in a brightly lit, busy hallway
options.D: Surprising the child quickly so they do not have time to worry

explanation: Awesome choice! Visual schedules take away the scary unknown by showing pictures of what will happen step-by-step. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why is advance care planning so important for older adults?

options.A: It guarantees that residents will never experience physical pain
options.B: It ensures the resident's personal wishes for end-of-life care are known and honored
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to communicate with grieving relatives
options.D: It legally forces family members to pay for expensive surgeries

explanation: Talking about preferences early on ensures that future medical decisions truly reflect what the resident wants when they can no longer speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h7)

question: What is a major danger of giving a child too many breaths during resuscitation?

options.A: Causing immediate permanent brain damage from too much oxygen
options.B: Lowering the child's heart rate into normal ranges
options.C: Preventing the lungs from ever collapsing
options.D: Increasing intrathoracic pressure and reducing blood return to the heart

explanation: If you bag a child too fast or too hard, you trap too much pressure inside their chest. That extra pressure actually blocks blood from flowing back to the heart. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of these nursing actions is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Screening adults for high blood pressure at a clinic
options.B: Tracing contacts of a patient with active tuberculosis
options.C: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.D: Administering routine vaccines to healthy children

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts—like giving immunizations to healthy kids. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which of these is the best example of an intangible cost in health care?

options.A: Hospital room rental fees
options.B: Pain and emotional suffering
options.C: Cost of surgical instruments
options.D: Lost wages from missing work

explanation: Intangible costs are the emotional and physical toll of sickness, like pain, stress, and worry. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h4)

question: What severe childhood malnutrition condition can happen when protein foods are restricted for too long?

options.A: Hypertension and stroke
options.B: Acute appendicitis
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Kwashiorkor or marasmus

explanation: When a child's diet lacks proper protein and calories over time due to strict taboos, it sadly paves the way for protein-energy malnutrition like kwashiorkor. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h5)

question: An HIV-positive mum looks worried and stressed about her infant feeding choices. What should be your very first step as a student nurse?

options.A: Build trust and provide a safe space to discuss her fears and questions
options.B: Tell her immediately that formula feeding is the only acceptable choice
options.C: Hand her a detailed textbook on virology and let her read independently
options.D: Involve her extended family in the discussion without her prior consent

explanation: Wonderful nursing instinct! Always start by creating a warm, judgment-free space where she feels safe to share her worries before diving into clinical advice. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T12#GNS216_U6_T12_h6)

question: Which of the following is considered a common vehicle for disease transmission?

options.A: Air currents in a closed hospital room
options.B: Direct skin-to-skin touch with a patient
options.C: A mosquito bite during the evening hours
options.D: Contaminated drinking water supplies

explanation: Water, food, and blood are common vehicles capable of carrying pathogens to a large group of people simultaneously. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main job of anthelminthic medications?

options.A: To replace lost red blood cells
options.B: To lower elevated systemic blood pressure
options.C: To kill or expel parasitic worms
options.D: To prevent bacterial wound infections

explanation: You've got this! Anthelminthics are simply the specific drugs we use to clear parasitic worm infections from the body. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is a standard metric used to check the quality of home health care?

options.A: The brand of uniforms worn by the nursing staff
options.B: Frequency of internal staff birthday parties
options.C: Total number of parking spaces at the agency office
options.D: Rates of unplanned hospital readmissions

explanation: Tracking readmission rates tells us a lot: if patients keep returning to the hospital, it might mean home care plans need tweaking to keep them stable. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T7#GNS324_U2_T7_h7)

question: If an abscess cavity has been packed with gauze, when is the patient usually asked to return for a check-up?

options.A: In one month for suture removal
options.B: Only if severe pain returns
options.C: After exactly two full weeks
options.D: Within 24 to 48 hours

explanation: Patients with packed wounds need a quick follow-up in 1 to 2 days so the healthcare team can check the healing and start removing the packing material. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T4#GNS311_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which nutrient is especially critical for adolescents experiencing rapid growth spurts and expanding blood volume?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Iron

explanation: Iron is needed to make hemoglobin for the extra red blood cells produced during adolescent growth spurts. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you must do if you realize a medication error has reached a patient?

options.A: Assess the patient's clinical condition and notify the physician
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to see if any symptoms develop
options.C: Hide the empty medication wrapper inside your uniform pocket
options.D: Resign from your nursing position immediately out of guilt

explanation: Patient safety always comes first. Check on the patient right away and get the doctor's help to manage any unexpected reactions. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which healthcare indicator looks at the physical setup, equipment, and staffing levels of a ward?

options.A: Process indicator
options.B: Outcome indicator
options.C: Balancing indicator
options.D: Structure indicator

explanation: Structure indicators look at the 'building blocks' or setup you have ready—like staff numbers, beds, and equipment available to deliver care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T5#GST319_U4_T5_h3)

question: A clinic is fully stocked with vaccines, but mothers refuse to bring their babies because nurses shout at them. What type of barrier is this?

options.A: Geographical distance barrier
options.B: Financial cost barrier
options.C: Environmental sanitation barrier
options.D: Attitudinal and service delivery barrier

explanation: Poor staff attitude creates a psychological barrier that prevents people from accessing care, even when supplies and physical locations are adequate. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h6)

question: When the penis is resting (flaccid), what do the helical arteries do?

options.A: They pump high volumes of blood directly into the dorsal veins
options.B: They remain constricted to limit blood flow into the sinusoids
options.C: They provide somatic sensation to the skin of the penis
options.D: They actively secrete nitric oxide to maintain tissue relaxation

explanation: Well done! When resting, these arteries stay tightly clamped down so that only a small amount of blood enters. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T4#GNS121_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why should a nurse worry if a patient stays on a clear fluid diet for days without extra nutrition?

options.A: The patient will lose all ability to swallow solid food forever.
options.B: The patient will quickly develop severe high blood pressure.
options.C: The patient's kidneys will immediately stop producing urine.
options.D: The patient is at high risk for malnutrition and delayed healing.

explanation: Without proteins and proper calories, wounds won't close and the body grows weak. Clear fluids are strictly short-term! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe assumption when reading study conclusions?

options.A: Statistical significance does not always mean clinical importance
options.B: Researchers should openly state the limitations of their work
options.C: A small trial on ten healthy young men proves the treatment works safely for elderly pregnant women
options.D: A well-designed randomized trial with a large sample provides strong evidence

explanation: Assuming results from a narrow, specific group apply to completely different populations is an error known as overgeneralization. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h5)

question: Even if a woman has received the HPV vaccine, why must she still go for regular cervical cancer screening later in life?

options.A: The vaccines do not protect against all high-risk strains of HPV
options.B: Screening tests are required to check if the vaccine was absorbed
options.C: Vaccinated individuals have a higher risk of developing infections
options.D: The vaccine wears off completely after exactly five years

explanation: Spot on! While the vaccine defends against the most common cancer-causing HPV strains, other less common high-risk strains can still cause issues, making regular screening still necessary. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)

question: Why is good nutrition and protein especially vital for patients healing from deep wounds like pressure sores?

options.A: Cells need building blocks to repair the extracellular matrix and regenerate tissue
options.B: Nutrition stops nervous tissue from sending pain signals to the brain
options.C: Vitamins automatically clean bacteria out of closed body cavities
options.D: Proteins completely replace the need for blood circulation in wounds

explanation: Your body can't rebuild damaged tissue out of nothing! Good protein gives cells the raw materials they need to patch things up. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why might a doctor order a CA-125 blood test for a patient with an ovarian mass?

options.A: To diagnose a sudden bacterial infection in the pelvis
options.B: To check if the patient is currently pregnant
options.C: To help check for markers associated with ovarian cancer
options.D: To measure the exact amount of estrogen in the blood

explanation: CA-125 is just a protein marker in the blood that can go up when certain ovarian growths are present. It helps doctors get a clearer picture! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h4)

question: What is a major reason why patients struggle to take antiretroviral therapy over a long period?

options.A: Lack of available water in the community
options.B: Doctors changing the prescription daily
options.C: Daily pill fatigue and complex routines
options.D: Automatic expiration of medicine bottles

explanation: The requirement to take medications every single day for the rest of one's life often leads to exhaustion and missed doses. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h3)

question: If you notice stagnant water sitting outside a house, which part of the epidemiological triad does this represent?

options.A: The susceptible host factor
options.B: The pathogenic agent factor
options.C: The environmental factor
options.D: The direct transmission factor

explanation: Well done! Stagnant water is an external physical condition around us that helps mosquitoes breed, making it an environmental factor. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T76#GNS214_U1_T76_h2)

question: Why do you pull the skin taut instead of pinching it before an intradermal injection?

options.A: Taut skin makes the needle sharper as it enters
options.B: Pinching causes severe bruising around the injection site
options.C: Pinching the skin lifts it and accidentally creates a subcutaneous pocket
options.D: Pulling the skin taut numbs the nerve endings temporarily

explanation: Well done! Pinching bunches up the fatty layer underneath, making it way too easy to accidentally slide past the dermis. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T8#GNS125_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why is the primary survey performed in a strict ABCDE order?

options.A: To make patient charting faster for the nursing staff
options.B: Because it is required by hospital administrative policy
options.C: To prevent the doctor from entering the room too early
options.D: To address the most life-threatening conditions first

explanation: The framework prioritizes vital body systems so that airway and breathing issues are resolved before moving to less urgent checks. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h2)

question: What type of language should a nurse use when writing home care notes?

options.A: Brief and casual phrases to save time
options.B: Objective, specific, and measurable details
options.C: General summaries and personal opinions
options.D: Emotional descriptions of the family dynamic

explanation: You got it! Stick to clear, factual observations so any other nurse reading your notes knows the exact status of the patient. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why is taking off (doffing) your PPE safely such a big deal for nurses?

options.A: To comply with clothing fashion standards in the hospital
options.B: To speed up the process of leaving an isolation room
options.C: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused by another staff member
options.D: To prevent self-contamination from pathogens resting on the outer surface

explanation: The outside of your gown and gloves is covered in germs! If you take them off clumsily, you'll accidentally spread those germs right onto your skin or scrubs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h4)

question: Why is it important to include a data analysis plan in your research proposal?

options.A: To allow the hospital pharmacy to order more medication supplies
options.B: To calculate the exact travel expenses of the research team
options.C: To ensure that no patients ever experience physical pain
options.D: To prove that the collected data can actually answer the research questions

explanation: Showing your analysis plan ahead of time proves your study is well-thought-out and that your results will actually answer your research questions. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h8)

question: How should a nurse correct a writing error in a paper health record?

options.A: Tear out the entire page of the notebook and start the report over
options.B: Draw a single line through the error, write 'mistaken entry', sign, and date it
options.C: Scratch out the wrong words heavily with a pen until no one can read them
options.D: Use correction fluid (tipp-ex) to completely cover the mistake until invisible

explanation: Using a single line preserves readability of the original error, preventing suspicions of tampering or hidden alterations. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h8)

question: What physical sign in the inner eyelids or nail beds is a classic warning sign of possible anemia?

options.A: Erythema
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Pallor
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: Spot on! Pale (pallor) inner eyelids and nail beds tell us hemoglobin levels might be low, which is a classic sign of anemia. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h7)

question: A client with a new physical disability refuses their medications and seems very hopeless. What does this most likely point to?

options.A: Unaddressed emotional distress impacting their treatment plan
options.B: A simple misunderstanding of the medication dosage schedule
options.C: An allergic reaction to the newly prescribed drugs
options.D: Normal adjustment that requires no nursing intervention

explanation: When clients give up or refuse care, it's often a cry for help. Deep emotional pain can get right in the way of managing physical health. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the job of the thermopile inside an infrared thermometer?

options.A: It blocks bright room light from entering
options.B: It warms up the lens to match body heat
options.C: It pumps cool air over the computer chips
options.D: It converts absorbed heat into an electrical signal

explanation: Think of the thermopile as a translator: it takes the focused heat energy and turns it into an electrical voltage that the thermometer's screen can read. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of establishing a clear case definition in surveillance?

options.A: Determining the exact cost of hospital treatment for insurance claims

options.C: Fulfilling administrative paperwork requirements without clinical value
options.D: Ensuring everyone uses the exact same criteria to identify a disease

explanation: A standard case definition ensures that health workers across different regions are counting the exact same illness criteria. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h5)

question: A student has stomach cramps and diarrhea after drinking from the school tap. Which part of the school environment failed here?

options.A: Academic evaluation standards
options.B: Physical environment safety
options.C: Psychosocial climate safety
options.D: Curriculum design policy

explanation: Well done! Safe drinking water is a basic part of the physical school environment, so bad water means a breakdown in physical safety. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of Tai Chi for older adults at risk of falling?

options.A: It rapidly increases total body bone density
options.B: It improves balance through slow, controlled movements
options.C: It eliminates the need for any assistive devices
options.D: It cures chronic joint inflammation in the knees

explanation: Tai Chi trains neuromuscular control and core stability, making it one of the most effective exercises for fall prevention. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h5)

question: What is the most common cause of anaemia among pregnant women in Nigeria?

options.A: Rapid bone marrow aging
options.B: Not getting enough iron and folate in food
options.C: White blood cells destroying each other
options.D: Drinking too much water daily

question: Where are the kidneys located in the human body?

options.A: Attached directly to the underside of the liver
options.B: Suspended freely within the lower pelvic cavity
options.C: Inside the peritoneal cavity near the stomach
options.D: Retroperitoneal against the back abdominal wall

question: What do we mean by patient harm in a clinical setting?

options.A: Worsening of a disease despite receiving correct medical treatment
options.B: Natural progression of an illness without any medical intervention
options.C: Discomfort felt by a patient waiting too long in the reception
options.D: Damage caused by healthcare management instead of the disease

explanation: Patient harm happens because of the care given by healthcare workers, not because of the natural course of the sickness itself. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T8#GNS312_U5_T8_h1)

question: While in a helicopter, your intubated patient suddenly becomes restless and starts breathing very fast. What should you check first?

options.A: The exact mileage remaining until the destination
options.B: Airway security and oxygen saturation levels
options.C: The patient's personal identification documents
options.D: Whether family members signed the consent forms

explanation: Sudden restlessness and fast breathing usually mean the patient isn't getting enough oxygen. Always check the airway and oxygen levels immediately! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h6)

question: A patient with a spinal cord injury has frequent bladder spasms. Which drug class is the provider most likely to order?

options.A: Anticholinergics
options.B: Loop diuretics
options.C: Urinary analgesics
options.D: Antibiotics

explanation: When nerve damage causes the bladder to spasm uncontrollably, anticholinergics help relax that detrusor muscle. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T5#GNS223_U8_T5_h3)

question: Why must you write down any recent antibiotics the patient is taking on the lab request form?

options.A: The laboratory requires proof that the prescription was filled
options.B: Medications can affect microbial growth and test interpretation
options.C: Pharmacies will not process the sample without this record
options.D: It determines the financial cost billed to the patient

explanation: Antibiotics in the patient's system can stop germs from growing in the lab dish, so the lab needs to know so they don't misread a false negative! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h5)

question: Which deficiency condition is marked by severe muscle wasting and very little body fat?

options.A: Night blindness
options.B: Goiter
options.C: Kwashiorkor
options.D: Marasmus

explanation: You're doing great! Marasmus is a severe lack of energy and protein where a child looks extremely thin and wasted away because of absent body fat. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h6)

question: Why does the human body need food nutrients?

options.A: To completely prevent all known infectious diseases
options.B: To speed up the physical digestion of solid wastes
options.C: To increase the total volume of blood in circulation
options.D: To provide substances needed for energy, growth, and repair

explanation: Think of nutrients as the fuel and building blocks your body uses every single day to stay active, grow, and heal wounds. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T009#GNS227_U1_T009_h1)

question: What is the primary reason for recommending a low-sodium diet in cardiac prevention?

options.A: It prevents the liver from producing too much cholesterol
options.B: It reduces fluid retention and lowers blood pressure
options.C: It stops the pancreas from releasing excess insulin
options.D: It increases the amount of dietary fiber in the gut

explanation: Excess sodium holds extra fluid in the blood vessels, increasing the pressure against arterial walls and forcing the heart to work harder. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h3)

question: A nurse wants to study a rare condition affecting only one person in the country every decade. Which rule does this study break?

options.A: Theoretical framework
options.B: Feasibility
options.C: Historical accuracy
options.D: Ethical acceptability

explanation: If there aren't enough participants available to study within a reasonable time, the project simply isn't feasible. Spot on! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h7)

question: How can rude or harsh behavior by staff at a receiving hospital negatively affect the referral system?

options.A: It discourages patients and their relatives from seeking formal care in the future
options.B: It improves communication between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: It makes patients recover faster because they want to leave early
options.D: It encourages villagers to build more primary health care centers

explanation: Negative attitudes create a hostile environment, causing patients to avoid hospitals and patronize unqualified providers instead. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: What is the medicalisation of FGM?

options.A: Using modern local anesthesia during traditional FGM rites
options.B: Performing FGM using trained healthcare workers in clinical settings
options.C: Treating the physical complications of FGM in a hospital
options.D: Researching surgical ways to reverse FGM damage

question: What is a major risk associated with using unregulated herbal mixtures?

options.A: Lowered financial costs for the family
options.B: Immediate cure of all psychiatric disorders
options.C: Permanent immunity to infectious diseases
options.D: Organ toxicity from incorrect dosing

explanation: True dat! Without standardized measurements or quality control, traditional herbal mixtures can sometimes cause accidental poisoning and organ damage. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h5)

question: If a patient is severely dehydrated with low blood pressure, which hormones will their body release to help?

options.A: Large amounts of filtered glucose
options.B: Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone
options.C: Decreased amounts of all electrolytes
options.D: Atrial natriuretic peptide only

explanation: Correct! Both aldosterone and ADH team up to hold onto salt and water, boosting your blood volume and cutting down urine output when you're dry. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why are taking baseline vital signs so important at the start of care?

options.A: To determine the patient's insurance coverage
options.B: To replace the need for taking a medical history
options.C: To compare against future readings to detect sudden changes
options.D: To calculate the exact date of patient discharge

explanation: Baselines give you a starting point. Later on, you can check new numbers against this baseline to spot if your patient is suddenly getting worse or improving. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h5)

question: What is the main reason newborns frequently develop mild physiological jaundice in the first few days of life?

options.A: Rapid destruction of white blood cells
options.B: An allergic reaction to early breast milk feeds
options.C: Bacterial colonization of the large intestine
options.D: Immature liver enzymes processing red blood cells

explanation: A newborn's liver is still maturing and cannot quickly process the large volume of bilirubin created when extra fetal red blood cells break down. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h2)

question: Why might a developing country have a GDP that is higher than its GNP?

options.A: The government spends more money on imported medical equipment
options.B: Citizens are working fewer hours in local clinics
options.C: Inflation rates are lower than neighboring countries
options.D: Foreign companies own a large share of domestic production and send profits abroad

explanation: When foreign firms generate massive output inside a country, it boosts local GDP, but those profits leave the country, keeping GNP lower. [learn more](GST322_U3_T1#GST322_U3_T1_h4)

question: What does an elevated reticulocyte count in a routine blood test usually indicate in a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Iron supplements are building up to toxic levels in the blood
options.B: The patient is experiencing a sudden kidney infection
options.C: The spleen has successfully cleared all abnormal cells from circulation
options.D: The bone marrow is working hard to replace destroyed red blood cells

explanation: Reticulocytes are newly formed red blood cells. A high count shows the bone marrow is rushing to make new cells to make up for those lost to haemolysis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: Which of these duties is a key part of system accountability in a hospital?

options.A: Notifying the doctor immediately when vital signs drop
options.B: Providing adequate staffing levels and well-maintained equipment
options.C: Performing bedside patient identity checks before giving medication
options.D: Submitting an accurate incident report after an adverse event

explanation: Management's job is to supply safe tools and enough staff so nurses can provide great care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why is recent rectal surgery considered a strict contraindication for a flatus tube?

options.A: It disrupts healing surgical suture lines and causes injury

options.C: It permanently damages the anal sphincter muscles
options.D: It causes severe respiratory depression
