question: What do we call the process when cancer cells break away and travel to other parts of the body?

options.A: Apoptosis
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Initiation

explanation: Metastasis is just the medical term for cancer packing its bags and traveling through the blood or lymph to start a new tumor elsewhere. You're mastering the terms! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h2)

question: As a nurse, why should you explore a patient's cultural practices rather than just banning them?

options.A: Traditional practices replace the need for all modern antibiotic treatments
options.B: Patients are more likely to ignore advice that completely dismisses their traditional beliefs
options.C: Cultural practices are always scientifically proven to be beneficial for health
options.D: Hospital policies legally require nurses to perform traditional steam baths

explanation: Spot on! When we respect our patients' beliefs instead of judging them, they trust us more and are way more likely to listen to our health advice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T15#GNS312_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why do mucous membranes absorb medicines so quickly?

options.A: An absence of epithelial tissue
options.B: High levels of gastric acid
options.C: A thick outer layer of dry skin
options.D: A rich network of blood vessels

explanation: Think of mucous membranes like a busy market with delivery vans parked right at the gate! They have lots of tiny blood vessels close to the surface, so drugs get picked up and carried into the bloodstream in no time. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T15#GNS125_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why do pregnant women routinely get screened for STIs during early prenatal visits?

options.A: To eliminate common morning sickness symptoms during the first trimester
options.B: To determine the exact biological sex of the unborn infant
options.C: To prevent transmitting infections from the mother to the developing fetus
options.D: To cure congenital genetic abnormalities present at conception

explanation: Exactly! Catching and treating infections early protects the baby from complications during pregnancy and birth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why should you pre-test your IEC materials with a small group before mass printing them?

options.A: To sell the materials to community members to raise funds for the clinic
options.B: To ensure the messages are clear and culturally appropriate before full release
options.C: To satisfy government paperwork requirements without involving the community
options.D: To test the physical strength and durability of the printing paper

explanation: Pre-testing helps you catch confusing words or awkward pictures early, saving you from wasting time and money on materials that won't work. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h7)

question: What is the most common immediate complication right after an FGM procedure?

options.A: Osteoporosis in later adulthood
options.B: Severe bleeding and acute pain
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Spot on! Cutting sensitive genital tissue with basic tools typically causes immediate, heavy bleeding and intense pain. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h7)

question: About how long is a standard research abstract?

options.A: 50 words
options.B: 1000 words
options.C: 250 words
options.D: 500 words

explanation: An abstract is a quick, bite-sized summary—usually kept around 250 words so busy nurses can read it in a minute! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is an important rule for a nurse educator when bringing new technology into a lesson?

options.A: The technology must support the learning objective rather than act as a mere distraction
options.B: The digital tools must be replaced with brand-new equipment every single month
options.C: The students must build the computer software themselves before class begins
options.D: The educator should avoid speaking and let the computer teach the entire course

explanation: Tech is awesome, but it should always serve a clear purpose—helping you understand the nursing concept better, not just acting as a flashy distraction. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common risk factor for stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Obesity and excess body weight
options.B: Menopause and decreased estrogen levels
options.C: Frequent high-fluid intake throughout the day
options.D: Vaginal childbirth and multiple pregnancies

explanation: Drinking plenty of water is healthy! The real risk factors involve things that weaken pelvic support, like childbirth, hormonal shifts, or heavy pressure. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: Which chemical messengers in the brain play a major role in mood and depression?

options.A: Serotonin and norepinephrine
options.B: Insulin and glucagon
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Sodium and potassium

explanation: Well done! Serotonin and norepinephrine are key neurotransmitters that help regulate our mood. An imbalance here is a big part of why depression happens. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which government body regulates health insurance in Nigeria?

options.A: World Health Organization (WHO)
options.B: National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN)
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

explanation: The NHIA is the main body in Nigeria tasked with setting up, regulating, and promoting health insurance so everyone can access care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is the best way to protect patient privacy during data collection?

options.A: Replacing patient names with code numbers on data sheets
options.B: Leaving interview notebooks open on the nurses' station desk
options.C: Posting study results on public bulletin boards in the ward
options.D: Sharing patient diagnoses with visiting family members

explanation: Well done! Using code numbers instead of real names hides patient identities and keeps their personal information safe. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h6)

question: Where should a nurse begin looking when selecting a site for peripheral IV insertion?

options.A: As close to the shoulder joint as physically possible
options.B: Directly in the antecubital fossa of the dominant arm
options.C: On the most distal areas of the non-dominant hand or forearm
options.D: On the lower extremities near the ankle joints

explanation: Starting low on the non-dominant arm preserves higher vein sites for future use if the current line fails or needs replacement. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the main idea behind the Essential Medicines Concept?

options.A: The mandatory use of expensive imported brand-name drugs over generics
options.B: A select list of priority drugs that meet the healthcare needs of the majority
options.C: Stocking every single pharmaceutical formulation ever invented in every clinic
options.D: Allowing patients to dispense their own prescription drugs without guidance

explanation: Essential medicines are a carefully picked list of priority drugs that treat the most common health needs of everyday people effectively and cheaply. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge to healthy eating in low-resource settings?

options.A: Cultural beliefs restricting certain foods during illness
options.B: Poverty and rising market prices for fresh produce
options.C: Guaranteed year-round access to free imported organic foods
options.D: Lack of proper refrigeration and food storage facilities

explanation: Spot on! Free, imported organic foods are definitely not a common everyday reality for most people. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h6)

question: A hospitalized patient has acute salpingitis with pelvic pain and a mild fever. Which nursing position helps drain pelvic fluids downward?

options.A: Ice packs applied directly to the lower abdomen
options.B: Strict bed rest flat on her back
options.C: Trendelenburg position with feet elevated
options.D: Semi-Fowler's position

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Keeping the patient slightly upright helps infected fluids pool safely in the lower pelvis rather than spreading upward. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T24#GNS216_U5_T24_h7)

question: What is a great way to help busy clinic staff keep data accurate without burning them out?

options.A: Eliminate all documentation requirements permanently across all clinics
options.B: Increase the number of complex indicators they must track every hour
options.C: Punish staff publicly every time a single tally mark is out of place
options.D: Keep data collection tools simple and provide ongoing training on their value

explanation: When nurses understand *why* data matters and have simple tools to record it, reporting becomes much easier and accurate! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h7)

question: What is a major cause of unsafe injection risks in informal healthcare settings?

options.A: Mandatory training for birth attendants
options.B: Too much government checking of pharmacies
options.C: An oversupply of safety boxes
options.D: Not enough clean, single-use equipment available

explanation: When places lack a steady supply of cheap, disposable syringes, dangerous reuse habits can creep in. Community health education helps fix this! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h6)

question: What does healthy pink or red granulation tissue tell you about a wound?

options.A: A severe bacterial infection has taken over the site.
options.B: The wound is healing nicely with new blood vessel growth.
options.C: The tissue is dying and needs immediate surgery.
options.D: The dressing material is causing an allergic reaction.

explanation: Granulation tissue is packed with tiny new blood vessels. Seeing that healthy pink/red color is a huge nursing win! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h7)

question: Why must an endotracheal tube with an inflated cuff be placed in an unconscious patient before gastric lavage?

options.A: To keep the patient's mouth open wide during tube insertion
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the lavage fluid
options.C: To deliver extra oxygen straight to the stomach lining
options.D: To protect the airway and stop fluid from entering the lungs

explanation: Unconscious patients lose their protective swallowing and gag reflexes, so a cuffed airway tube creates a physical barrier against aspiration of stomach washings. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h4)

question: What does a cross-sectional study NOT do?

options.A: Measure variables at the same time
options.B: Describe community health issues
options.C: Collect data from a sample
options.D: Manipulate or change variables

explanation: Cross-sectional studies are purely observational. Researchers just watch and record; they don't interfere with treatments or change anything! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h2)

question: What happens if just one link breaks in the vaccine cold chain?

options.A: The vaccine automatically adjusts its own temperature
options.B: The vaccine potency can be permanently lost
options.C: The packaging becomes sterile automatically
options.D: The expiration date of the product extends

explanation: Vaccines are very delicate biological products. If they get too warm or too cold, they lose their power to protect—even if they look completely normal! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h1)

question: Why do early adolescents often look a bit uncoordinated or clumsy?

options.A: Neurological damage occurs temporarily during puberty
options.B: Hands and feet grow faster than the rest of the body
options.C: Shrinking of the inner ear balancing structures
options.D: Lack of proper physical exercise in school

explanation: Think of it like a growth spurt where the hands and feet shoot up first! This temporary mismatch throws off coordination for a bit, but it completely evens out. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a very common physical hazard you might find in a patient's home?

options.A: Standardized hospital call bells in every room
options.B: Sterile, bolted-down medical furniture
options.C: Continuous negative pressure isolation airflow
options.D: Frayed electrical cords and loose throw rugs

explanation: Everyday household items like loose rugs and damaged cords are top culprits for trips and falls in residential settings. Always watch out for them! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why must nurses understand basic inventory and stock control principles?

options.A: To design new storage shelves for the hospital
options.B: To negotiate better prices with medical suppliers
options.C: To take over the job of the hospital pharmacist
options.D: To prevent emergency supply shortages on the ward

explanation: Nurses handle ward supplies every day, so knowing stock rules helps them prevent running out of critical items during patient care. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h1)

question: According to cell theory, where do all new cells come from?

options.A: Spontaneous generation
options.B: Extracellular fluid
options.C: Nutrients in the blood
options.D: Pre-existing cells

explanation: Cell theory states that life is continuous because all new cells are formed by the division of older, pre-existing cells. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do we restrict fat in certain diets rather than cutting it out completely?

options.A: Completely removing fat causes immediate weight gain.
options.B: The body still needs a minimal amount of fat for essential functions.
options.C: Fat-free foods are too expensive to produce.
options.D: Patients will refuse to eat any food without fat.

explanation: Even on a low-fat diet, our cells and organs need a little bit of fat to function properly and absorb vital nutrients! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h1)

question: The principle of sustainability in CBR mainly encourages the use of what?

options.A: Local resources and affordable community strategies
options.B: Strictly cash-only payments for every clinic visit
options.C: Exclusively high-tech equipment imported from abroad
options.D: Temporary foreign volunteers who leave after one month

explanation: Sustainability means programs can continue running using materials, people, and funds that are readily available within the local environment. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why do nurses apply universal precautions to every patient, not just those with a known infection?

options.A: Hospital management requires it to save money on lab testing
options.B: Testing blood takes too many days to be useful in an emergency
options.C: Many individuals with infections may be completely unaware or undiagnosed
options.D: Patients get offended if nurses ask about their infection status

explanation: Spot on! Many people carry bloodborne viruses without knowing it, so treating every patient's fluids as potentially infectious keeps everyone safe. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h4)

question: Which question addresses how a nursing team will track their progress during a quality project?

options.A: What are we trying to accomplish?
options.B: How will we know that a change is an improvement?
options.C: Who is responsible for the nursing budget?
options.D: What change can we make that will result in an improvement?

explanation: Well done! This question pushes the team to choose clear signs and measures to prove if their new ideas are actually working. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why do we advise patients with peptic ulcers to eat smaller, more frequent meals?

options.A: It prevents large fluctuations in gastric acid secretion and stomach distension.
options.B: It speeds up the rate at which food empties into the large intestine.
options.C: It completely cures the bacterial infection without needing antibiotics.
options.D: It ensures that the liver produces enough bile for fat digestion.

explanation: Spot on! Small meals keep the stomach from stretching too much and stop huge waves of acid from flooding the stomach all at once. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary advantage of the intravenous route over oral administration?

options.A: Absence of local site pain
options.B: Simpler technique for nurses
options.C: Faster onset of drug action
options.D: Lower risk of fluid overload

explanation: Injecting fluids directly into the bloodstream skips the digestive system, allowing medications to work almost immediately. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h1)

question: In the ward, what do we call a non-living object—like a BP cuff or a table—that can transfer germs?

options.A: A living insect that transmits a parasite to humans
options.B: A type of protective mask worn during surgery
options.C: An inanimate object that can transfer infectious agents
options.D: An antibiotic resistant strain of hospital bacteria

explanation: That's a fomite! Any non-living surface or object that picks up germs and passes them to the next patient is a fomite. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h4)

question: What is the main job of global health funding groups like Gavi or the Global Fund?

options.A: Collecting local taxes from rural market traders to build city hospitals
options.B: Enforcing strict criminal laws against medical malpractice in private clinics
options.C: Directly managing the daily nursing schedules of government health workers
options.D: Pooling resources from multiple sources to buy vaccines and medicines on a large scale

explanation: These global funds collect money from various countries to buy large quantities of essential medicines and vaccines for developing nations. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h3)

question: Why do the ureters enter the bladder wall at a slant (oblique angle)?

options.A: To allow the renal pelvis to drain more fluid at one time
options.B: To act as a valve that stops urine from flowing backward
options.C: To shorten the overall length of the lower ureter tract
options.D: To slow down fluid speed before it enters the bladder cavity

explanation: You're doing great! That slanted angle acts like a one-way valve, keeping urine from washing back up to the kidneys when the bladder fills up. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T2#GNS121_U2_T2_h4)

question: How can poor food storage at home harm a child's health?

options.A: It lowers the market price of local vegetables.
options.B: It reduces the child's daily physical activity levels.
options.C: It automatically increases the vitamin content of stored grains.
options.D: It causes foodborne infections that trigger diarrhea and hinder nutrient absorption.

explanation: Spot on! Spoiled or contaminated food leads to tummy infections, making it hard for the child's body to keep the nutrients it needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h6)

question: Which health areas in Nigeria have traditionally received the most support from international donor agencies?

options.A: Geriatric care facilities for retired politicians
options.B: Private cosmetic surgery and dental implant clinics
options.C: Orthopedic workshops for sports injuries
options.D: Infectious diseases, immunization, and maternal health programs

explanation: Global partners like WHO or USAID heavily target public health priorities like HIV/AIDS, malaria, and vaccines. Keep this public health focus in mind! [learn more](GST322_U4_T3#GST322_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main reason a nurse dilutes a medicated lotion?

options.A: To change the color of the cream
options.B: To decrease its active concentration
options.C: To make the container last longer
options.D: To speed up the drying process

explanation: Dilution lowers the percentage of the active drug so it is gentler on sensitive skin. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h1)

question: Which medication group forms the first step of the WHO analgesic ladder?

options.A: Strong agonists like fentanyl
options.B: Pure antagonists like naloxone
options.C: Intravenous muscle relaxants
options.D: Non-opioids like paracetamol

explanation: For mild pain, we always start simple at Step One with basic non-opioids like paracetamol or ibuprofen, plus an adjuvant if needed. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why is the time spent bathing a patient so great for building the nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: It forces the patient to follow every single hospital rule without arguing
options.B: It gives the patient a chance to voice hidden fears and ask questions
options.C: It allows the nurse to complete all nursing documentation for the shift
options.D: It proves to the doctor that the nurse can complete physical tasks quickly

explanation: Spot on! That quiet, one-on-one time makes patients feel safe and cared for, often opening up about worries they wouldn't share in a busy hallway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h1)

question: You are asked to do a complex procedure you were never taught in school. What should you do?

options.A: Ask a junior student nurse to perform the task instead
options.B: Decline the task and inform the supervisor about lacking training
options.C: Perform the task anyway to avoid upsetting the senior doctor
options.D: Read a quick internet article on the phone and do the procedure

explanation: Never work outside your scope of practice! Speak up and protect your patient (and your license) by admitting what you don't know yet. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h7)

question: What is a nurse's main goal in family-centered HIV care?

options.A: To empower the family with tools to sustain health
options.B: To isolate the patient from family stress entirely
options.C: To take over all daily decision-making for the household
options.D: To manage hospital financial accounts and billing

explanation: Spot on! Nurses provide education and encouragement so families can manage care confidently on their own. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h7)

question: Facing discrimination over a long period of time causes which physical response in the body?

options.A: Enhanced muscle growth and physical strength
options.B: Persistent stress and elevated cortisol levels
options.C: Permanent immunity to common infections
options.D: Immediate decrease in blood pressure

explanation: Discrimination acts as a constant stressor, keeping stress hormones like cortisol high and wearing down a person's health over time. Keep learning! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h5)

question: Which of these is a core nursing responsibility when providing family planning supplies?

options.A: Providing confidential counseling and accurate dispensing
options.B: Performing major surgical procedures for sterilization
options.C: Setting international pricing policies for pharmaceuticals
options.D: Manufacturing the contraceptive hormones in the laboratory

explanation: As a nurse, your role is to guide clients with privacy, answer questions, and hand out chosen supplies safely. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h8)

question: What is a major cause of clinical errors when patients are being transferred between care teams?

options.A: Excessive time spent resting on duty
options.B: Overuse of basic patient hygiene supplies
options.C: Strict adherence to written safety checklists
options.D: Communication breakdowns during handovers

explanation: Spot on! Poor communication during shift changes or patient transfers often leads to missed details, making handovers a high-risk moment for mistakes. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why can it be a bit misleading to call every test in an LFT panel a 'function' test?

options.A: They can only be performed after a surgical liver biopsy
options.B: Some markers measure cell damage rather than actual working capacity
options.C: They measure waste products filtered exclusively by the kidneys
options.D: They only measure the gallbladder and not the liver tissue

explanation: Great thinking! Tests like transaminases actually show us if liver cells are injured or leaking, rather than directly measuring how much work the liver can do. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T11#GNS221_U2_T11_h1)

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) tell us?

options.A: Total calories burned during a strenuous two-hour workout
options.B: Percentage of body fat compared to lean muscle mass
options.C: Maximum amount of food a person can digest in one day
options.D: Minimum calories needed to maintain basic life functions at rest

explanation: BMR is your body's resting engine speed—the bare minimum calories needed just to keep your organs ticking while you rest. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h7)

question: In what direction should you clean a female patient's perineal area before putting in a catheter?

options.A: From back to front
options.B: From side to side vigorously
options.C: From front to back
options.D: In a circular outward motion

explanation: Correct! Always wipe from front to back (toward the back passage) so you don't drag any germs from the anus toward the urethral opening. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h6)

question: Why do family members often encourage pregnant women to follow strict local food rules?

options.A: To prevent complications like a baby growing too large for a normal delivery
options.B: To reserve expensive food items exclusively for the village elders
options.C: To ensure the mother maintains a high level of physical fitness
options.D: To comply with modern international nutritional guidelines

explanation: You got it! Most food taboos come from well-meaning family members trying to keep the baby small so delivery will be easier. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h4)

question: A patient tells you they feel extremely panicked and short of breath at the thought of entering a narrow, enclosed scanner. What is your best first action?

options.A: Tell the patient to close their eyes and ignore the fear
options.B: Cancel the appointment permanently without consulting anyone
options.C: Force the patient into the scanner quickly to get it over with
options.D: Acknowledge the fear and report the need for an anti-anxiety medication order

explanation: You're a caring nurse! Validating their fear and helping arrange for medication or an open MRI makes the experience much better. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h4)

question: How do high birth rates directly impact hospital maternity wards in busy areas?

options.A: They create an excess of sterile delivery equipment
options.B: They decrease the need for newborn immunization supplies
options.C: They cause severe overcrowding and strain available nursing staff
options.D: They eliminate the occurrence of postpartum complications

explanation: Spot on! Too many deliveries at once stretch hospital beds and overworked nurses to their limits. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h7)

question: A conscious patient refuses to take their prescribed medication. What should you do first?

options.A: Threaten to discharge them immediately from the ward
options.B: Crush the drug into their food without telling them
options.C: Force the medication into their mouth for their own good
options.D: Explore their reasons and notify the prescriber

explanation: Patients always have the right to say no. Take a moment to listen to their worries and let the doctor know, rather than forcing anything. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h4)

question: If a patient sues a nurse for malpractice, what is the very first thing they must prove about their connection to the nurse?

options.A: That a professional duty of care existed between the nurse and patient
options.B: That the nurse intended to cause deliberate physical harm
options.C: That the hospital facility lacked an active accreditation
options.D: That the nurse was working past the scheduled shift time

explanation: Before a court can look at negligence, it must first be established that you were actually the nurse assigned to care for that patient—that's the duty of care! [learn more](GST322_U4_T9#GST322_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is the most common condition treated using genito-urinary anticholinergics?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Urinary tract infection
options.C: Overactive bladder
options.D: Kidney stone formation

explanation: Overactive bladder—marked by sudden, intense urges to pee—is the number one reason these drugs are given. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T5#GNS223_U8_T5_h3)

question: Which professional has special training to help couples work through emotional and intimacy problems?

options.A: Orthopedic surgeon
options.B: Emergency room registrar
options.C: Phlebotomy technician
options.D: Certified sex therapist

explanation: Sex therapists have specialized training to guide couples through psychological and emotional intimacy bumps on the road. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T27#GNS312_U1_T27_h7)

question: A snakebite patient starts bleeding spontaneously and has abnormal clotting lab results. Which toxin is likely at work?

options.A: Myotoxins
options.B: Hemotoxins
options.C: Neurotoxins
options.D: Cytotoxins

explanation: Think 'hemo' for blood! Hemotoxins mess with the body's clotting system, causing bleeding and messy lab results. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h2)

question: How does severe malnutrition affect drugs that normally bind strongly to albumin?

options.A: It increases free, active drug in the blood, raising toxicity risk
options.B: It forces the drug to store permanently in bone marrow
options.C: It makes the blood-brain barrier open to everything
options.D: It causes the liver to destroy the medicine immediately

explanation: Without enough albumin (due to poor nutrition), there are fewer taxi cabs for the drug. This leaves too much free medicine floating around, which can lead to accidental overdose. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why is active psychosis or severe mania a reason to hold off on granting leave?

options.A: Hospital rules strictly forbid patients with mood disorders from leaving
options.B: Family members never want to visit patients with mood disorders
options.C: Insurance companies refuse to pay for medications during outings
options.D: The patient lacks the stability and impulse control needed to stay safe in the community

explanation: When symptoms are still acute and uncontrolled, being outside a secure hospital can put the patient or others at risk. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h4)

question: What triggers the extrinsic pathway of the coagulation cascade?

options.A: The rapid destruction of red blood cells in the spleen
options.B: Direct contact of blood with exposed collagen inside a vessel
options.C: Tissue factor released from damaged outside tissues
options.D: An increase in white blood cell counts during an infection

explanation: The extrinsic pathway is set in motion quickly when tissue factor leaks from injured cells outside the blood vessel. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: How is the grey matter and white matter arranged inside the developing spinal cord?

options.A: White matter forms internally and gray matter forms externally
options.B: Sensory fibers are kept completely outside the spinal column
options.C: Gray matter forms internally and white matter forms externally
options.D: Motor neurons develop only within the outer white matter

explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cord is neatly organized with nerve cell bodies on the inside (grey matter) and nerve fiber tracts on the outside (white matter). [learn more](GNS211_U3_T1#GNS211_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient with a mild fever and routine vaccination needs visits a nearby facility staffed by community health workers. Which level of care is this?

options.A: Quaternary level of care
options.B: Tertiary level of care
options.C: Secondary level of care
options.D: Primary level of care

explanation: Spot on! Community clinics handling everyday things like immunizations and mild fevers are right at the primary care level. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h1)

question: What is the primary design feature of a Shakir tape used in child health?

options.A: It has built-in electronic Bluetooth sensors
options.B: It uses color-coded zones to screen for malnutrition
options.C: It is made of stretchy elastic for comfortable fitting
options.D: It measures body height instead of limb circumference

question: Which of these practices helps stop clinical errors during tricky or high-risk procedures?

question: Where in the breast do most cancers actually start growing?

question: Which gland produces melatonin to help control your sleep cycle?

question: How many weeks of pregnancy make up a normal term delivery?

question: Why is prevalence data most useful for community health nurses?

question: What makes home health care nursing ethically different from hospital nursing?

question: What does 'food security' mean for a population?

options.A: Storing a ten-year supply of grains in underground bunkers

question: A patient is tracking her ovulation using an over-the-counter urine test kit. Which hormone is the kit primarily designed to detect?

question: Which specialized structure inside the ventricles makes cerebrospinal fluid?

question: How does the body primarily generate heat when exposed to cold environments?

question: Why should you check back in after a conflict has supposedly been settled?

question: When is a patient usually switched from a first-line ART regimen to a second-line regimen?

question: What does 'cultural humility' mean for a home health nurse?

options.A: Recognizing personal biases and respecting the patient's cultural beliefs
options.B: Ignoring cultural differences to treat everyone identically
options.C: Reading a textbook about a culture before every visit
options.D: Convincing the patient to adopt the nurse's personal lifestyle

explanation: It's all about checking your own biases at the door and keeping an open mind about how a patient's background shapes their health choices. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which special cells in the lining of the intestine make protective mucus?

question: Which piece of equipment is usually missing on a standard ship?

options.D: Basic digital blood pressure cuffs

question: A patient comes in with a small plastic bead stuck in their ear, but no pain. What is your very first step?

question: What is a major challenge when using wearable health devices in some Nigerian communities?

question: How do family planning 'supply methods' differ mainly from long-acting methods like coils or implants?

options.B: They provide permanent sterilization after a single use

question: What is a major benefit of using an epidural for pain relief during labor for a patient with sickle cell disease?

question: A male patient is getting a semen analysis for fertility checks. What should you tell him to do beforehand?

question: Where do you mostly find muscarinic receptors in the human body?

question: What is the main benefit of regular team meetings among different healthcare professionals in an SNF?

question: How do chronic stressors differ from acute stressors?

question: What is a major advantage of longitudinal research over cross-sectional studies?

question: In the popular SOAP charting format, what does the letter 'O' stand for?

question: What is the primary maternal function of human chorionic gonadotropin in early pregnancy?

question: What is 'moral distress' in nursing?

options.D: The sadness a nurse feels when a patient passes away peacefully

question: Why do certain cultural practices place strict food bans on women during pregnancy?

question: You just finished giving an IM injection on the ward. What is the safest thing to do right away?

question: Why is drawing a community map so useful for health planning?

question: When is the best time for a pregnant woman to come in for her first booking visit?

question: What is the main job of the fluid inside serous membranes?

question: Why is it important to discover the exact reason a caregiver stopped immunizing?

question: How do distribution bottlenecks contribute to micronutrient deficiencies in remote communities?

question: What is the main type of tissue found in the hypodermis (the layer right under the skin)?

question: Why shouldn't nurses just give anti-malarials immediately to every patient with a fever without testing first?

question: A head nurse wants to keep the ward staff motivated and aware of patient safety goals. Where is the run chart typically displayed for maximum team impact?

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a quality improvement team?

question: A patient with a new leg cast complains of severe, burning pain that does not respond to prescribed pain medication and has pale toes. What is the nurse's priority action?

question: In SOAP charting, what kind of details go into the 'O' (Objective) section?

question: Why do we routinely give iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant women?

question: Why does our body reabsorb most digestive fluids further down the intestines?

question: What is the main purpose of synovial fluid in a joint?

question: Which expense usually takes up the biggest slice of a hospital's budget?

question: What are unexplained fevers, night sweats, and weight loss in lymphoma called?

question: Which action must happen BEFORE the ambulance begins moving with a trauma victim?

question: A nurse teaches mothers why immunization prevents killer childhood diseases. Which learning domain is this mainly addressing?

question: What are the four steps in the PDSA quality improvement cycle?

options.A: Plan, Do, Study, Act
options.B: Prepare, Diagnose, Solve, Assess
options.C: Prevent, Document, Stop, Analyze
options.D: Predict, Delegate, Secure, Audit

explanation: Remember PDSA: Plan your change, Do it on a small scale, Study the results, and Act on what you learned! [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h7)

question: Nursing informatics is a cool blend of three major fields. Which ones make up this specialty?

options.A: Biology, chemistry, and health administration
options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Nursing theory, public health, and data analytics
options.D: Pharmacology, anatomy, and computer engineering

explanation: Spot on! Nursing informatics brings together nursing science, computer science, and information science to help us manage health data like pros. You'll see this tech in action everywhere on the wards! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for growing and branching the milk ducts during early development?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Estrogen acts like the master gardener, helping the milk duct system grow and branch out nicely inside the breast. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h2)

question: Opened in 1907, which facility was Nigeria's very first psychiatric institution?

options.A: Uselu Psychiatric Hospital
options.B: Yaba Asylum
options.C: Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Enugu
options.D: Aro Neuropsychiatric Hospital

explanation: Yaba Asylum in Lagos was built during colonial times, starting out mainly as a place to keep and watch over mentally ill individuals. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which bloodborne infection has the highest risk of spreading after just one accidental needle-stick?

options.A: Hepatitis B virus
options.B: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B is super infectious and carries the highest transmission risk after a needle prick. Another reason to be extra careful! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which nursing action helps prevent skin breakdown caused by oxygen mask straps?

options.A: Apply strong medical adhesive tape directly to the forehead
options.B: Remove the mask permanently and stop all oxygen therapy
options.C: Place protective padding under pressure points and check skin often
options.D: Pull the elastic straps tighter so the mask never shifts

explanation: Padding shares the load evenly across the skin, and checking frequently lets you spot irritation before it turns into a wound. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T11#GNS212_U2_T11_h7)

question: What is one major perk of condoms over hormonal birth control pills?

options.A: Condoms require no action at the time of intercourse
options.B: Condoms cause permanent changes in fertility
options.C: Condoms have a much higher real-world perfection rate
options.D: Condoms offer protection against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: You got it! While pills are great for preventing pregnancy, only barrier methods like condoms protect against STIs too. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: A ward nurse carefully checks expiry dates and avoids opening extra sterile packs during a procedure. What is the nurse showing?

options.A: Risk pooling
options.B: Equity
options.C: Efficiency
options.D: Vertical integration

explanation: Spot on! Preventing waste in the ward is a practical way nurses practice efficiency every single day. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h2)

question: When should nutritional screening typically happen for a newly admitted hospital patient?

options.A: Right before the patient is discharged home
options.B: At the final weekly multidisciplinary meeting
options.C: Only after the patient requests a meal tray
options.D: Within twenty-four hours of admission

explanation: Early screening within the first day helps catch risks before the patient's condition deteriorates. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h4)

question: Which vitamin supplement is routinely given to pregnant mothers to prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Iron

explanation: Spot on! Folic acid is vital for early cell division and helps prevent serious birth defects of the brain and spine. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T1#GNS211_U3_T1_h7)
